comparisons.peer_topic: Investment structure and accounting method for tax credit VIEs
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm invests in nonconsolidated tax credit VIEs via limited partnership interests to receive income tax credits and benefits. As of January 1, 2024, the firm adopted ASU No. 2023-02, electing the proportional amortization method for qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects receiving production tax credits, with amortization and credits recorded in the provision for taxes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose investments in unconsolidated tax credit VIEs structured as limited partnerships where a third party controls significant activities. BAC reports total assets of $85.7 billion for these VIEs, while GS describes the investment strategy of acquiring income tax credits through these limited partnerships without providing a specific total asset figure for the VIEs in the selected text, but confirms the identical governance structure where 'a third-party is typically the general partner or the managing member' (GS) versus 'An unrelated third party is typically the general partner or managing member' (BAC).

sentences.text: The Corporation holds equity investments in unconsolidated limited partnerships and similar entities that construct, own and operate affordable housing, renewable energy and certain other projects.
The total assets of these unconsolidated tax credit VIEs were $85.7 billion and $84.1 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.
An unrelated third party is typically the general partner or managing member and has control over the significant activities of the VIE.
The firm makes equity investments in nonconsolidated tax credit VIEs that invest in qualified affordable housing and renewable energy projects.
These VIEs are generally organized as limited partnerships or similar entities and a third-party is typically the general partner or the managing member.
The firm invests in the entity as a limited partner and receives income tax credits and other income tax benefits for such investments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Tax credit vehicle investment structure and exposure
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm holds investments in unconsolidated tax credit vehicles for affordable housing, alternative energy, and other projects, with a maximum loss exposure of $35.2 billion at December 31, 2024, of which $15.0 billion was unfunded. Risk is mitigated by withholding capital until projects qualify for tax credits.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) hold investments in unconsolidated tax credit VIEs focused on affordable housing and energy projects, characterized by limited partnership structures where unrelated third parties hold controlling interests, preventing consolidation. While BAC quantifies the total assets of these VIEs at $85.7 billion, JPM quantifies its maximum loss exposure (equity investments and funding commitments) at $35.2 billion. Both disclosures explicitly state that a third party is the general partner or managing member with control over significant activities, leading to non-consolidation.

sentences.text: The Corporation holds equity investments in unconsolidated limited partnerships and similar entities that construct, own and operate affordable housing, renewable energy and certain other projects.
The total assets of these unconsolidated tax credit VIEs were $85.7 billion and $84.1 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.
An unrelated third party is typically the general partner or managing member and has control over the significant activities of the VIE.
The Firm holds investments in unconsolidated tax credit vehicles, which are limited partnerships and similar entities that own and operate affordable housing, alternative energy, and other projects.
These entities are primarily considered VIEs.

A third party is typically the general partner or managing member and has control over the significant activities of the tax credit vehicles, and accordingly the Firm does not consolidate tax credit vehicles.
The Firm generally invests in these partnerships as a limited partner and earns a return primarily through the receipt of tax credits allocated to the projects.

comparisons.peer_topic: Tax equity investment interests in low-income communities and renewable energy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm invests in tax equity interests from entities developing low-income housing and renewable energy facilities, entitling it to shares of the generated tax credits and losses.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and Morgan Stanley (MS) engage in tax equity investments in entities developing low-income housing and renewable energy facilities to generate tax credits. BAC categorizes these primarily as unconsolidated tax credit VIEs with $85.7 billion in total assets, whereas MS describes its interest as 'tax equity investment interests' entitling it to shares of tax credits and losses. Both firms invest in these specific project types (housing and renewable energy) to capture tax benefits, though BAC emphasizes the VIE accounting classification and asset size while MS focuses on the nature of the equity interests and credit allocation.

sentences.text: The Corporation holds equity investments in unconsolidated limited partnerships and similar entities that construct, own and operate affordable housing, renewable energy and certain other projects.
The total assets of these unconsolidated tax credit VIEs were $85.7 billion and $84.1 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.

The Firm invests in tax equity investment interests issued by entities that develop and own low-income communities (including low-income housing projects) and entities that construct and own facilities that will generate energy from renewable resources.
The interests entitle the Firm to a share of tax credits and tax losses generated by these projects.
